Bread flour versus all purpose flour

The difference comes down to protein. Bread flour usually sits near twelve to fourteen percent, which builds more gluten and gives a chewy, tall loaf. All purpose flour is closer to ten or eleven percent and makes a softer crumb.

You can swap one for the other in most recipes. Expect a slightly denser result when you use all purpose flour in a loaf, and a slightly tougher cake when you use bread flour where a cake was meant.

If you only have all purpose flour, add a spoonful of vital wheat gluten per cup and the loaf will rise closer to what the recipe intended.
